entries.name: C
entries.definition: A general-purpose procedural programming language created by Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs in the early 1970s.

entries.name: Carib
entries.definition: A Cariban language spoken by the Kalina (Kari'nja) people along the coasts of northern South America.

entries.name: Castilian Spanish
entries.definition: The standard variety of the Spanish language as spoken in Spain, especially in its central and northern regions.

entries.name: Catalan
entries.definition: A Romance language spoken mainly in Catalonia, the Balearic Islands, Valencia and Andorra, where it is the official language.

entries.name: Cebuano
entries.definition: An Austronesian language spoken mainly in Cebu, the central Philippines and parts of Mindanao.

entries.name: CFML
entries.definition: A tag-based scripting language, run by servers such as Adobe ColdFusion and Lucee, for building dynamic web applications.

entries.name: Chakma
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken by the Chakma people in Bangladesh and India.

entries.name: Chamorro
entries.definition: An Austronesian language spoken by the Chamorro people of Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands.

entries.name: Chichewa
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken mainly in Malawi and also known as Nyanja, notably in Zambia.

entries.name: Chinese
entries.definition: A group of related Sinitic languages, including Mandarin and Cantonese, spoken mainly in China and written in Chinese characters.

entries.name: Chipmunk Basic
entries.definition: A free BASIC interpreter for several platforms, based on classic Microsoft-style BASIC.

entries.name: CLIST
entries.definition: A scripting language for writing command procedures under IBM's TSO on z/OS and earlier MVS mainframe systems.

entries.name: Clojure
entries.definition: A dynamic, functional Lisp dialect that runs mainly on the Java Virtual Machine, created by Rich Hickey.

entries.name: COBOL
entries.definition: A business-oriented programming language dating from 1959, still used in banking, insurance and government mainframe systems.

entries.name: CoffeeScript
entries.definition: A programming language with concise syntax that compiles to JavaScript.

entries.name: COMIT
entries.definition: An early string-processing programming language developed at MIT in the 1950s for linguistic research and machine translation.

entries.name: Common Lisp
entries.definition: A standardized, multi-paradigm dialect of Lisp specified in ANSI standard X3.226-1994.

entries.name: Component Pascal
entries.definition: A programming language in the Pascal and Oberon tradition, a refinement of Oberon-2 designed by Oberon microsystems.

entries.name: Crystal
entries.definition: A statically typed, compiled programming language with a Ruby-inspired syntax.

entries.name: C#
entries.definition: The C# programming language.

entries.name: CSS
entries.definition: Styling web documents with cascading style sheets.

entries.name: Cython
entries.definition: A programming language that is a superset of Python and is compiled to C to build fast Python extension modules.

entries.name: Czech
entries.definition: A West Slavic language spoken mainly in the Czech Republic.

entries.name: D
entries.definition: A general-purpose systems programming language with C-like syntax, created by Walter Bright.

entries.name: Danish
entries.definition: A North Germanic language, the official language of Denmark.

entries.name: Dari
entries.definition: The variety of Persian that is an official language of Afghanistan.

entries.name: Dart
entries.definition: A programming language developed by Google, used mainly with the Flutter framework to build apps for several platforms.

entries.name: Delphi
entries.definition: An object-oriented dialect of Pascal (Object Pascal) and the development environment built around it, originally from Borland and now from Embarcadero.

entries.name: Dhivehi
entries.definition: The Indo-Aryan language of the Maldives, written in the Thaana script.

entries.name: Digital Command Language
entries.definition: The command language of the OpenVMS operating system and its predecessors from Digital Equipment Corporation, used interactively and for command procedures.

entries.name: Dinka
entries.definition: A Nilotic language spoken by the Dinka people of South Sudan.

entries.name: Duala
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken in and around the city of Douala in Cameroon.

entries.name: Dutch
entries.definition: A West Germanic language spoken mainly in the Netherlands, Belgium and Suriname.

entries.name: Dylan
entries.definition: A multi-paradigm, object-oriented programming language derived from Scheme and influenced by Common Lisp, developed in the 1990s by Apple and partners.

entries.name: Dzongkha
entries.definition: A Sino-Tibetan language, the national language of Bhutan.

entries.name: ECMAScript 2015
entries.definition: The 2015 edition of the ECMAScript standard on which JavaScript is based, which added classes, modules, arrow functions and promises.

entries.name: Eiffel
entries.definition: An object-oriented programming language designed by Bertrand Meyer and built around design by contract.

entries.name: Elixir
entries.definition: A dynamic, functional programming language that runs on the Erlang virtual machine.

entries.name: Elm
entries.definition: A functional programming language that compiles to JavaScript, used to build web front ends.

entries.name: English
entries.definition: The English human language; not a programming language.
